state:
- NUP98 selection is itself an unsupplied premise that is never flagged: [S1] supports only a link between TDP-43 aggregates and 'pore/nucleoporin components' generically, not NUP98 specifically, yet the answer labels only the kinase and sites as assumptions. Fix: explicitly list 'NUP98 is the relevant phosphorylated FG-nucleoporin in ALS' as a speculative bridge, and add a Phase-0 phospho-occupancy screen across all FG-Nups so a phospho-null at the wrong target cannot be misread as rejecting the mechanism class.
- Falsification prong (i) is confounded by detection limits: NUP98 is gly-rich/low-complexity and FG-repeat peptides are poor mass-spectrometry substrates, and low-stoichiometry interphase phosphorylation may sit below assay sensitivity, so 'no preceding phosphorylation' could be a technical negative. Fix: include a mitotic-arrest positive control for the mapping pipeline and site-occupancy standards, so prong (i) is interpretable as biological absence rather than missed signal.
- Phase 1 mixes C9orf72-expansion lines into the TDP-43-mechanism temporal mapping despite [S2] showing C9orf72 has repeat-RNA-driven transport routes of its own: an early NUP98 phosphorylation rise in those lines could reflect C9-specific stress signaling, contaminating the precedence test. Fix: designate pure TDP-43 (e.g., mutant TDP-43) isogenic lines as the primary mapping cohort and use C9orf72 lines only as external-validity checks with separate interpretation.
